text: What if you dug 200 meters under the bank that stores $800 billion in gold?
You start on the sidewalk, right outside the Federal Reserve.
Soon, it's solid Manhattan rock.
Then water starts seeping in from the walls.
The vault sits eighty feet down. That's below sea level.
You'd need a pump running day and night just to stay dry.
Then you hit a thick wall of concrete.
Behind it? Over six thousand tons of gold.
Behind a door that weighs ninety tons.
Now picture the alarms going off.
The Fed even has its own police force.
Then come the helicopters overhead.
And then the FBI shows up.
Federal law says up to twenty years in prison.
But here's the twist. That gold doesn't even back your money.
Open your wallet. There's no gold in there.
Not since nineteen seventy-one, when the U.S. stopped exchanging dollars for gold.
Today, you just walk up to an ATM.
The bank approves it, and cash comes out.
An armored truck keeps that machine full.
Your balance drops. The gold doesn't move an inch.
Meanwhile, your digger is stuck, and the police are pulling it out.
Total haul? Zero gold, and one very muddy shovel.
So, gold or a bank balance, which would you rather have? Comment one.
